generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, describing and reflecting differ. A log can record what happened in a session, or it can ask why an athlete responded as they did, or why your own coaching manner shaped how the group trained. Sport subjects reach this judgement differently, a biomechanist from motion data, a coach from what they saw on the pitch, a manager from participation figures, but each rewards the reflection that reaches a reason over the account that only reports. Sport assessment, from coaching logs to lab reports, asks for the same.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching students write a reflection on the same coaching assessment, a session they each delivered that came back with a lower mark than they expected.

Tom writes that the session lost marks on organisation and that the feedback said the warm-up ran too long and the main drill felt rushed. This is accurate, and it is entirely description: it reports what happened and what the feedback said, but it does not ask why the warm-up overran or what Tom did that led to it. The account stops at what happened.

Amara starts from the same facts, then reflects: the warm-up overran because she had planned too many activities and would not cut any once the session was live, so the main drill lost the time it needed. The low mark was not bad luck but a consequence of that planning. That is a reflection: it reaches a reason, and it points to her own decisions.

Both described the same session accurately. Only Amara reflected on it, by asking why it happened and what her own part was.
generatedProse.summary: Description answers 'what happened'; reflection answers 'so what' and 'why', looking back critically at your own actions and decisions. You can now explain the difference, tell one from the other in a sport example, and deepen a thin reflection by asking why something happened and what your part in it was. The next lesson takes the understanding you reach and turns it into action.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's account a reflection rather than a description?

items.text: She reached a reason for the low mark and pointed to her own planning shaping the session.
She reported the feedback more accurately than Tom.
She wrote at greater length about the session.
She felt more strongly about the mark.

feedback.correct: That's right. Reaching a reason for the mark, and pointing to her own approach, is what makes it a reflection.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara worked out, beyond reporting the feedback.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara reflected by reaching a reason for the low mark and pointing to her own planning. Accurate reporting, extra length or a stronger feeling are all still description.
